chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abu al-Khattab, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him)

Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'And monasticism which they invented for themselves, which We did not prescribe for them, except to seek the pleasure of Allah,' he said: 'The night prayer.'
ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic term 'monasticism' (rahbaniyyah) refer to in Shia interpretation?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), the concept of 'monasticism' (rahbaniyyah) mentioned in Surah Al-Imran is interpreted not as a foreign innovation but as the established Sunnah of night prayer (salat al-layl). This interpretation aligns with Shia exegetical tradition, which often views the Quranic critique of monasticism as a rejection of excessive asceticism rather than voluntary worship itself, thereby legitimizing the night prayer as a divinely endorsed spiritual discipline.
